durability as sustainability — one set instead of replacing yearly

picks.name: The Wellness Optimizer
picks.why_plausible: She tracks sleep and pays premiums to improve it, and the brief's one hard functional claim — actually breathable linen — speaks directly to temperature regulation at night; price_sensitivity: low with a $95 AOV stretches to a considered bedding purchase.
lean_into: outcome-focused: sleeping cooler, fewer night wakeups
transparency about the material itself — pure linen, nothing coated or blended
avoid: overstated clinical or 'scientifically proven sleep' claims the brand can't back
picks.ad_angle: Linen breathes in a way cotton percale can't — the cheapest upgrade to how you sleep hot.

plan.summary: A deliberately narrow plan: budget leans on Hearthstone Goods, where new-home and gifting life events make premium linen a natural next purchase, with a secondary test on Marlowe & Co.'s quality-driven affluent women; Northbed is out as a direct bedding competitor and everything else lacks a purchase-moment link or sits far below the $260 order.

recommended.name: Hearthstone Goods

signals.name: audience
signals.detail: ages 28-48 cover 72% of 30–55; high income for premium price

recommended.tier_reason: The score only saw a weak kitchen/home-textiles tag link and undercounted the purchase moment in the notes: this checkout is explicitly a new-home / nesting or gifting moment, which is exactly when people buy premium bedding, and the basket size already supports a $260 order.
recommended.rationale: Notes say "Gifting and new-home life events drive purchase" for high-income cookware buyers at a $198 basket, so a shopper outfitting a new home is a natural next buyer of premium linen sheets; the sustainability-motivated framing also suits natural-fibre, made-in-Portugal messaging.

evidence.quote: Gifting and new-home life events drive purchase

recommended.risk: Only 2.8M monthly impressions, so volume will be thin and results slow to read; the $260 first order is assumed and may be well above a single sheet-set trial price.

test.name: Marlowe & Co.

signals.name: audience
signals.detail: ages 45-65 cover 40% of 30–55; high income for premium price

test.tier_reason: Off-category is right about the basket but the notes describe precisely the buyer this brand targets: older affluent women who respond to quality messaging rather than DTC hype, at 8.4M impressions with a $112 basket that makes a $260 order only 2.3x.
test.rationale: Notes say "Older affluent women. Lower impulse but high AOV. Responds to quality messaging." which matches an audience that "got tired of the Brooklinen/Parachute aesthetic"; worth testing whether quality-led linen copy converts off an apparel checkout.

test.risk: The connection is demographic, not a purchase adjacency, and the notes flag "Lower impulse" — a $260 bedding order at an apparel confirmation page may simply not be an impulse these shoppers make.

campaign.name: Breathable linen bedding made in portugal · post-purchase launch

bid_strategy.rationale: $260 first order (assumed) × 0.30 = $78.00 target CPA: one-time purchase, so the first order has to pay back the acquisition. The max CPA allows headroom while the campaign learns over 14 days.

test_plan.hypothesis: Notes say "Older affluent women. Lower impulse but high AOV. Responds to quality messaging." which matches an audience that "got tired of the Brooklinen/Parachute aesthetic"; worth testing whether quality-led linen copy converts off an apparel checkout.
test_plan.risk: The connection is demographic, not a purchase adjacency, and the notes flag "Lower impulse" — a $260 bedding order at an apparel confirmation page may simply not be an impulse these shoppers make.
test_plan.promote_if: CPA at or below the $78.00 target after 14 days: move it to core.
test_plan.cut_if: CPA above the $101.40 maximum, or no conversions after 14 days: stop it.

frequency_cap.rationale: Offers appear once, right after checkout; repeating them reads as spam.

experiment.graduate_rule: After 14 days, move a test publisher to core if its CPA is at or below target; cut any placement above max CPA.
experiment.notes: Creatives rotate evenly until each has enough conversions to compare.

launch_summary.summary: $8,500 of the $10,000 budget goes to Hearthstone Goods, where new-home and gifting moments make premium linen a natural next purchase, running gift, sustainability and breathability angles. A $1,500 test on Marlowe & Co. checks whether quality-led "made in Portugal" copy converts off an apparel checkout with older affluent women; it moves to core at or below the $78.00 target cost per new customer and stops above $101.40. Northbed was excluded as a direct bedding competitor.
uncertainties: The $260 first order value is assumed, and the $78.00 target cost per new customer is built directly on it.
The Marlowe & Co. link is demographic rather than a purchase adjacency, and their notes flag lower impulse buying against a $260 order.
One-time purchasing is assumed, so the first order alone has to pay back acquisition; real margin and repeat rate would change the target.
questions: What is your actual average first order value?
Do customers typically buy again, or is this genuinely a one-time purchase?
What margin can you afford to spend on acquiring a new customer?
